needs_result.text: Proposed and prototyped an MCP-based agentic tool in Python (FastMCP, Ollama gpt-oss:20b, PostgreSQL, GitHub Actions CI), presented in a live stakeholder demo.
Designed hierarchical agent workflows with real-time query capabilities, integrating Exograph and PostgreSQL for persistent storage and retrieval across agent sessions.

Proposed the request flow: a user's text goes through the API and a customised prompt to the MCP server, where one LLM instance writes GraphQL queries against the client's Convex database and a second instance runs the statistical analysis before the result returns to the user.

Designed reproducible scikit-learn pipelines with feature engineering (temporal features, interaction terms, target encoding), model selection, cross-validation and hyperparameter tuning across classification and regression tasks.

Working independently for India-based startups and individual clients, built agentic RAG workflows (LangChain, LangGraph, ChromaDB) on GCP Cloud Run, NLP pipelines (Hugging Face Transformers, Ollama) and scikit-learn pipelines, served ML models as REST APIs (FastAPI, Docker), and contributed to a team LoRA fine-tune of a Llama model.

Shipped features in a production fintech (financial-services) application as part of a team: integrated Twelve Data (real-time market feeds) and Plaid (bank linking, transaction imports) via REST APIs, with SSL pinning and AWS Cognito SSO.

As a trainee, modelled user-profile, transaction-history and event-booking data in Core Data schemas with CRUD and session-state management, and automated a manual data-collection process with a JavaScript web-scraping pipeline that surfaced market-trend signals used for pricing decisions.
Predicted bank-customer churn with a supervised XGBoost propensity classifier in R (tidymodels): two-stage Bayesian hyperparameter tuning, SMOTE inside the preprocessing recipe and MCC evaluation.

Needed a voice assistant that answers in real time and can be interrupted: built it end to end as a full-stack application (React front end, FastAPI and Google ADK back end, full-duplex WebSocket) with ReAct-based agent orchestration, barge-in handling and self-hosted speech models on Docker/CUDA (float16 inference, model warm-up) to cut latency.

bullets.text: Wrote a three-tier test framework (tool-level, API/integration, live agent) of ~65 tests across 8 files, validated across the LLM provider migration from Groq to AWS Bedrock after a rate-limit evaluation.

Diagnosed where it struggled with a three-tier, ~65-test evaluation harness (tool-level → API → live) and hallucination-rate analysis, debugging failures layer by layer, and used the same harness to validate the Groq to Bedrock migration after a rate-limit evaluation.

bullets.entry: CoverFit — insurance benchmarking API (Bristol × UWE AI Hackathon)
bullets.text: An insurance sponsor needed a fast, low-cost, explainable benchmark (hackathon brief): paired a deterministic matching engine (FastAPI, pandas, Pydantic) with a single LLM call (Gemini via LiteLLM) for the rationale, covered by pytest tests; responses arrive in under 3 seconds at ~£0.003 per query.

bullets.entry: GTAI Cell Line Finder — multi-omics graph for cancer cell-line selection (PoC)
bullets.text: Integrated 14 public omics source files into one graph of 1,399 cell lines and 16,385 genes, cut RAM from 8.2 to 5.5 GB on a free T4 GPU, reported the weak results openly (train Pearson 0.807 vs test 0.545) and debugged a hash-randomisation bug to its root cause.

Needed an agent that researchers could trust on a cancer research platform, including when its tools fail: built a tool-calling agent (LangChain, Claude Haiku 4.5 on AWS Bedrock) for three use cases (gene alias resolution, prompt-engineered explanations of a fixed scoring pipeline, validated dataset descriptions), with deterministic Ensembl and HGNC calls, deterministic hallucination guards, and circuit breakers with a 19,213-gene parquet fallback for when the external APIs are unavailable.

bullets.entry: llama3-8b-qlora-math-t4 — QLoRA fine-tuning of Llama 3.1 8B for maths under a token budget
bullets.text: Needed to know what fine-tuning can change in an 8B model on a free 15 GB GPU: QLoRA-fine-tuned Llama 3.1 8B (4-bit, Unsloth, TRL) training 0.52% of its parameters, which under a fixed 384-token budget raised answer completion from 32% to 52% and exact-answer accuracy from 16.2% to 27.3% on held-out NuminaMath problems (n=99).
